results.name: random_set_inrange_breadth
results.description: In 3-4 example sets spanning >=40 where no final digit and no parity is shared by more than n-2 examples (no near-rule), yes rate for non-example targets inside the set's range; observed above null means people generalise broadly ('anything in range') from rule-less noisy sets more than the model predicts, below means less.
results.code:
# name: random_set_inrange_breadth
# description: In 3-4 example sets spanning >=40 where no final digit and no parity is shared by more than n-2 examples (no near-rule), yes rate for non-example targets inside the set's range; observed above null means people generalise broadly ('anything in range') from rule-less noisy sets more than the model predicts, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    u = pd.unique(s)
    codes = pd.Categorical(s, categories=u).codes
    U = np.full((len(u), 4), np.nan)
    for i, x in enumerate(u):
        v = [int(float(z)) for z in x.split(",") if z.strip() != ""][:4]
        U[i, :len(v)] = v
    E = U[codes]
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    Ed = np.mod(E, 10)
    td = np.mod(t, 10)
    shares_last = np.any(Ed == td[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    in_set = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    Ep = np.mod(E, 2)
    n_even = np.sum(Ep == 0, axis=1)
    n_odd = np.sum(Ep == 1, axis=1)
    lastE = E[np.arange(len(E)), np.maximum(n - 1, 0)]

    cnt = np.stack([np.sum(Ed == d, axis=1) for d in range(10)], axis=1).max(axis=1)
    par = np.maximum(n_even, n_odd)
    noisy = (n >= 3) & (hi - lo >= 40) & (cnt <= n - 2) & (par <= n - 2)
    m = noisy & ~in_set & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: small_vs_large_far_target_asymmetry
results.description: Among targets >15 from every example that share no final digit with any example, yes rate for small targets (<=15) minus large targets (>=85); observed above null means people favour small numbers far from the examples more than the model predicts (a small-number / compressed-scale bias the model lacks).

    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()

    Ed = np.mod(E, 10)

results.name: outlier_position_parity_rule_contrast
results.description: In >=3-example sets where exactly one example differs in parity from the rest, yes rate for non-example targets of the majority parity when the odd-one-out is shown FIRST minus when it is shown LAST; observed above null means a first-position stray undermines the rule less (relative to a last-position one) for people than the anchored-first-example model predicts, below means more.
results.code:
# name: outlier_position_parity_rule_contrast
# description: In >=3-example sets where exactly one example differs in parity from the rest, yes rate for non-example targets of the majority parity when the odd-one-out is shown FIRST minus when it is shown LAST; observed above null means a first-position stray undermines the rule less (relative to a last-position one) for people than the anchored-first-example model predicts, below means more.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    u = pd.unique(s)
    codes = pd.Categorical(s, categories=u).codes
    U = np.full((len(u), 4), np.nan)
    for i, x in enumerate(u):
        v = [int(float(z)) for z in x.split(",") if z.strip() != ""][:4]
        U[i, :len(v)] = v
    E = U[codes]
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    Ed = np.mod(E, 10)
    td = np.mod(t, 10)
    shares_last = np.any(Ed == td[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    in_set = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    Ep = np.mod(E, 2)
    n_even = np.sum(Ep == 0, axis=1)
    n_odd = np.sum(Ep == 1, axis=1)
    lastE = E[np.arange(len(E)), np.maximum(n - 1, 0)]

    one_out = (n >= 3) & ((n_even == 1) | (n_odd == 1))
    maj = np.where(n_even > n_odd, 0, 1)
    out_par = 1 - maj
    first_out = one_out & (Ep[:, 0] == out_par)
    last_par = np.mod(lastE, 2)
    last_out = one_out & (last_par == out_par)
    tgt = ~in_set & (np.mod(t, 2) == maj)
    a = first_out & tgt
    b = last_out & tgt
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: digit_reversal_target_yes
results.description: Yes rate for targets that are the digit reversal of a two-digit example (e.g. 38 for 83, not itself an example) minus yes rate of other non-example targets at a similar distance (3-30 from every example) sharing no final digit with any example; observed above null means people use digit-reversal similarity the model lacks.

# name: digit_reversal_target_yes
# description: Yes rate for targets that are the digit reversal of a two-digit example (e.g. 38 for 83, not itself an example) minus yes rate of other non-example targets at a similar distance (3-30 from every example) sharing no final digit with any example; observed above null means people use digit-reversal similarity the model lacks.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    u = pd.unique(s)
    codes = pd.Categorical(s, categories=u).codes
    U = np.full((len(u), 4), np.nan)
    for i, x in enumerate(u):
        v = [int(float(z)) for z in x.split(",") if z.strip() != ""][:4]
        U[i, :len(v)] = v
    E = U[codes]
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    Ed = np.mod(E, 10)
    td = np.mod(t, 10)
    shares_last = np.any(Ed == td[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    in_set = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    Ep = np.mod(E, 2)
    n_even = np.sum(Ep == 0, axis=1)
    n_odd = np.sum(Ep == 1, axis=1)
    lastE = E[np.arange(len(E)), np.maximum(n - 1, 0)]

    rev = np.mod(E, 10) * 10 + np.floor(E / 10)
    ok = (E >= 10) & (E <= 99) & (np.mod(E, 10) != 0) & (rev != E)
    is_rev = np.any(ok & (rev == t[:, None]), axis=1) & ~in_set
    base = ~in_set & ~shares_last & (dist >= 3) & (dist <= 30)
    a = is_rev
    b = base & ~is_rev
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: item_unanimity_rate
results.description: Fraction of (set, target) items answered >=3 times on which every answer is identical; observed above null means people are more consistent/extreme per item than the model's graded yes-probabilities predict (model too moderate), below means the model is overconfident.

# description: Fraction of (set, target) items answered >=3 times on which every answer is identical; observed above null means people are more consistent/extreme per item than the model's graded yes-probabilities predict (model too moderate), below means the model is overconfident.
def test_statistic(df):

    u = pd.unique(s)
    codes = pd.Categorical(s, categories=u).codes
    U = np.full((len(u), 4), np.nan)
    for i, x in enumerate(u):
        v = [int(float(z)) for z in x.split(",") if z.strip() != ""][:4]
        U[i, :len(v)] = v
    E = U[codes]
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    Ed = np.mod(E, 10)
    td = np.mod(t, 10)
    shares_last = np.any(Ed == td[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    in_set = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    Ep = np.mod(E, 2)
    n_even = np.sum(Ep == 0, axis=1)
    n_odd = np.sum(Ep == 1, axis=1)
    lastE = E[np.arange(len(E)), np.maximum(n - 1, 0)]

    key = s + "|" + df["target"].astype(int).astype(str)
    g = pd.DataFrame({"k": key.to_numpy(), "y": y}).groupby("k")["y"].agg(["size", "mean"])
    g = g[g["size"] >= 3]
    if len(g) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(((g["mean"] == 0) | (g["mean"] == 1)).mean())

    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)

    td = np.mod(t, 10)

results.name: nearest_first_vs_later_example_contrast
results.description: Among non-example targets in >=2-example sets that share no final digit with any example and lie within 15 of some example, yes rate when the nearest example is the FIRST one shown minus when the nearest is a later one; observed above null means people generalise around the first example by magnitude more than the model predicts (stronger primacy), below means less.
results.code:
# name: nearest_first_vs_later_example_contrast
# description: Among non-example targets in >=2-example sets that share no final digit with any example and lie within 15 of some example, yes rate when the nearest example is the FIRST one shown minus when the nearest is a later one; observed above null means people generalise around the first example by magnitude more than the model predicts (stronger primacy), below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    u = pd.unique(s)
    codes = pd.Categorical(s, categories=u).codes
    U = np.full((len(u), 4), np.nan)
    for i, x in enumerate(u):
        v = [int(float(z)) for z in x.split(",") if z.strip() != ""][:4]
        U[i, :len(v)] = v
    E = U[codes]
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    Ed = np.mod(E, 10)
    td = np.mod(t, 10)
    shares_last = np.any(Ed == td[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    in_set = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    Ep = np.mod(E, 2)
    n_even = np.sum(Ep == 0, axis=1)
    n_odd = np.sum(Ep == 1, axis=1)
    lastE = E[np.arange(len(E)), np.maximum(n - 1, 0)]

    D = np.abs(E - t[:, None])
    D = np.where(np.isnan(D), 1e9, D)
    nearest = np.argmin(D, axis=1)
    base = (n >= 2) & ~in_set & ~shares_last & (dist <= 15)
    a = base & (nearest == 0)
    b = base & (nearest > 0)
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())
